chunks: As for what Saʿd narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from ʿAbd al-Malik, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about turning in salat (prayer): does it invalidate the salat (prayer)? He said: No, but I do not like that you do it.

So the correct way regarding this report is that we interpret it as referring to one who does not turn toward what is behind him, but rather turns to the right and left; then this does not invalidate his salat (prayer), although he has left what is more excellent, according to what he explained in this report and other reports. And what further clarifies that will come.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer under discussion
key_terms.الِالْتِفَاتِ: turning or looking away during salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْأَفْضَلَ: what is superior or more virtuous to do

ai.seo_question: Does turning to the right or left during salat (prayer) invalidate the prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on turning during salat (prayer). It indicates that slight turning to the right or left does not invalidate the salat (prayer), though it is disliked and contrary to what is better. The concluding note explains that the report is to be understood as applying to turning that does not amount to fully turning backward.
